## The criteria — each scenario gets scored on six questions

| # | Criterion | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Re-run frequency | Automation pays back only on repetition; run-twice-a-year scenarios stay manual |
| 2 | Business risk | Money movement — totals, discounts, tax, inventory, order data — raises automation value |
| 3 | Determinism | Same inputs → same observable outcome, every run; flaky behavior gets stabilized first |
| 4 | Checkable assertion | "Pass" must be verifiable from a response body or DOM value, not human taste |
| 5 | Maintenance exposure | Prefer assertions below the UI (API/unit level) that survive redesigns |
| 6 | Environment dependency | Completing it needs a payment sandbox, 3DS auto-pass, or an interceptable email call |

Automate-first needs high scores across most of these; a scenario that fails criterion 4 or 6 outright goes to automate-later or manual regardless of how risky it is.

## How checkout scenario clusters typically land

🧪 **Automate first** — usually the largest cluster in a checkout plan:
- End-to-end purchase happy paths (guest + logged-in) — highest risk, re-run most often
- Total calculation: coupon application, discount stacking, tax, shipping cost — deterministic and mostly assertable at API level
- Validation negatives and boundaries: invalid/expired card format, empty required fields, quantity 0 / −1 / oversize, coupon expired or already redeemed
- Cart state: add/update/remove, persistence across login, stock guard against overselling
- Order integrity: created order matches cart contents and totals; confirmation email asserted via API or a mocked mail call
- Decline handling where sandbox decline codes are controllable

🚧 **Automate later** — right tier, infrastructure not ready:
- Payment completion including 3-D Secure — automatable only when test mode auto-passes it; otherwise automate up to "click Pay" and keep the final step manual. Your sandbox answer would have moved roughly a dozen typical scenarios between here and the tier above
- Visual-sensitive steps — after a visual-regression baseline exists, not before
- Anything currently unstable when run manually — automating instability bakes flakiness into the suite

🔍 **Stay manual** — each for a reason:
- UX judgment calls ("errors are clear", "flow feels smooth") — no machine-checkable oracle
- New-design visual review — automation compares to a baseline; new screens don't have one
- Exploratory and security probing (order-ID tampering, coupon abuse) — automation replays the known; exploration finds the unknown
- One-off or rare-setup scenarios — never pays back
- External-world handoffs: how the confirmation email renders in a real client, fulfillment, provider dashboard state
- Full accessibility audit — automate only the smoke checks (labels, focus, keyboard reachability)

## Working assumptions until you say otherwise

- **Purpose**: faster regression runs. If it's actually a CI gate, the first batch gets shorter and stricter on runtime and stability
- **Stack**: unknown. If no automation exists at all, the first batch shrinks to ~8–12 skeleton scenarios (login → cart → one happy purchase, one coupon rule, one validation negative, order integrity) so the suite gets built on scenarios that also prove the framework works
- **Payments**: unknown — every payment-completion scenario gets flagged "automate-first if sandbox allows" rather than silently placed

| Item | Budget | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Stage wall clock | 10:00 | Your constraint |
